notes.text: The owner attended the January 23rd meeting of the UH Bauer College Energy Committee (GEMI), chaired by Lane Sloan, with Dean Arthur Warga, Praveen Kumar, Bruce Williamson, Bob Peebler and others; next meeting proposed in about six weeks.
The Energy Committee agreed GEMI Partnership levels: Trustee $100,000, Partner $50,000, Investor $25,000, Sponsor $10,000; certificate placements of up to 10, 4, 2 and 0 respectively.

Dr. Kumar described three GEMI energy certificate programs starting in September: Risk Management, Energy Accounting, and International Project Finance (the last may need more development time). He asked members to name people to give feedback on course proposals.
Lane Sloan asked committee members for ideas on funding GEMI launch marketing, targeted at $200,000 for this year, since the annual fee cycle starting in September leaves a funding gap.

The committee discussed a Bauer College symposium on topics arising from the Enron collapse (clearing house, credit risk); Dr. Kumar will email members for input, then Dean Warga decides whether to pursue it.

Robert E. Brooks (GPCM Natural Gas Market Forecasting System, RBAC) reported in his 1/25/02 GPCM News that iterating between power models (Prosym, GE Maps, IREMM) and GPCM is impractical because the power models take too long to solve.

Robert E. Brooks recommends running the power model three times instead of once, with high, medium and low Henry Hub forward price trajectories plus basis estimates. The resulting three gas-burn/price points per location form a demand curve for GPCM.

Under Brooks' proposed method, GPCM solves for an interpolated expected price and gas-burn combination. A final power model run is then made using the GPCM prices, which should produce gas burns close to GPCM's values.
